reference.title: Band standing rear delt row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row, breathe in as the arms go back out.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s row, short squeeze, about 2 s back

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: you should be able to bring the elbows level with the back without leaning
prescription.progression: More reps, a longer squeeze, a step further from the rack, or a stronger band

cues.text: Loop the band round a rack upright at shoulder height. Face it, feet hip width, a strand in each hand, palms down, arms reaching forward.
Breathe out and row the elbows back and out wide, a little below shoulder height, forearms in line with the band.
Stop with the elbows just behind the shoulders, bent about 90 degrees; squeeze the shoulder blades together, shoulders down.
Breathe in and let the arms go back out slowly, keeping the band tight.
Brief pause with the arms long, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows tucking to the sides (a normal row)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows out wide, about 80 degrees from the trunk.
Stand tall; use a lighter band or step closer to the rack.
Keep the shoulders down as the elbows go back.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band pull the arms back fast

kinematics.norm: Upper arm about 60-90 degrees out from the trunk so the pull is a horizontal abduction; horizontal abduction loads the posterior deltoid more than a close row (Franke 2015)
From the arms reaching forward to the upper arms just behind the shoulders (clinical opinion)
Nearly straight at the bottom, about 90 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Overhand (palms down) is the usual rear delt row grip; on a reverse fly a neutral grip gave more posterior deltoid activity than a pronated one (Schoenfeld 2013)
Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest at the squeeze; at matched effort elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar activity in shoulder exercises (Andersen 2010)
Controlled, about 1 s out and 2 s back (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
Check the band for nicks or tears and loop it securely round the upright; a band that slips or snaps can hit the face.
Band tension is user-chosen: pick one you can row to the squeeze without leaning back.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: let the elbows come a little lower and closer to the body.
Low-back tension: soften the knees and brace the trunk; use a lighter band.
regressions: Lighter band or a step closer to the rack.
progressions: Stronger band or a step further back.
Band face pull (adds a turn-out at the end).

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: with the elbows out wide the row becomes a horizontal abduction (a bent-arm reverse fly). Horizontal abduction (reverse peck deck) gave much higher posterior deltoid activity than a close-elbow seated row (Franke 2015; Botton 2013).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Prime mover: with the elbows out wide the row becomes a horizontal abduction (a bent-arm reverse fly). Horizontal abduction (reverse peck deck) gave much higher posterior deltoid activity than a close-elbow seated row (Franke 2015; Botton 2013).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Pull the shoulder blades together at the end of the row.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Pull the shoulder blades together at the end of the row.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: External rotator that works with the posterior deltoid in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: External rotator that works with the posterior deltoid in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps hold the upper arms out wide.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps hold the upper arms out wide.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the elbow bend; less involved than in a close row because the elbows lead.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Holds the elbow bend; less involved than in a close row because the elbows lead.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright so the body does not lean back.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder blade; shrugging shifts work here.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder blade; shrugging shifts work here.
